messages:
Sophie (AE): Quick heads-up — Nimbus Health wants to run a week-long POC for a new model they forked: flint-13B-qlora-v2. Asking if we can (1) serve it via Redwood Hosted/Dedicated, (2) estimate latency on a 16k context, and (3) confirm any compatibility blockers for Private.
Sophie (AE): They picked that variant for medical finetune evals; license looks permissive but has a no-commercial-redistribution clause — flagged in their security questionnaire.
Ajay Patel: Re: runtime compatibility — does flint-13B use any exotic ops or FlashAttention variants? If it's standard Llama2-style weights + qlora quant, we should be fine but need to confirm kv cache format and tokenizer.
Lucas Reed: I can run a quick local build on our inference node. Sophie, can you drop the model manifest (weights URL + tokenizer name) here?
Sophie (AE): Sure — manifest: model_id: nimbus/flint-13b-qlora-v2, weights: s3://nimbus-models/flint-13b/qv2.bin, tokenizer: sentencepiece-flint. They provided a short README mentioning 8-bit QLoRA.
María Gómez: License note — security asked if we store customer-provided weights in Redwood object storage for Dedicated/private. For Hosted we can't re-distribute; we'll need a pointer and keep it customer-scoped. For Private we can allow local ingestion. Document that in the SQA response.
Ajay Patel: Ok thanks. I'll check kernel coverage. Quick checklist:
- tokenizer compatibility (sentencepiece)
- kv cache layout (standard: contiguous past_key/value)
- quant format (qlora 8-bit per-tensor?)
- fused attention kernel support

Lucas Reed: Running a compatibility smoke test now. Command I'm using:
```bash
# pull weights to test node
rdx-cli model fetch --id nimbus/flint-13b-qlora-v2 --to /tmp/models/flint13
# start local runtime with quant path
rdx-runtime --model /tmp/models/flint13 --max-seq 16384 --batch 8
```

Lucas Reed: First result: tokenizer loads, but sentencepiece vocab size is 32000 (fine). kv cache layout looks standard. However the qlora quant metadata uses "scales_per_group=128" which we need to verify support for our 8-bit path.
Ajay Patel: Scales per group 128 is ok for our dynamic quant unpacking — we have a fallback but performance will drop ~1.3x vs native 8-bit. For 16k context, latency per token on a single A100-80GB (dedicated) ballpark is ~18-25ms depending on batching. On p4d it's slightly slower per-token due to smaller memory; we'd recommend Dedicated with 80GB class GPU for 16k.
Sophie (AE): Nice. Client asked for an SLO: 95th percentile latency for chat (avg 800 token responses) under 500ms — is that realistic?
Ajay Patel: 800 tokens in 500ms is unrealistic for 13B at 16k context unless we use heavy batching and prefix caching. If most requests reuse prefixes and caching is effective, we could approach it for amortized throughput, but p95 per-request? no. We should set expectations: 
- p95 token latency ~20-30ms -> 800 tokens ~= 16-24s.
- For under 500ms, they'd need a smaller response size or a distilled model.

Sophie (AE): I'll relay that. Also pricing question — they want an estimate for Dedicated reserve: 4x80GB GPUs with throughput for approx 300 concurrent chat sessions. Any rough $/month we can ballpark?
Lucas Reed: I'll estimate offline, but quick calc: cost is heavily dominated by infra + reserved nodes. Engineering we usually base on tokens/sec and GPU utilization; I'll send a spreadsheet.
María Gómez: Security point — the SQA asks if we run static scans on third-party weights. We don't currently do weight signing verification for customer-supplied files in Hosted. We should mark that as a known gap and propose a mitigation (isolate in customer tenant, audit logs, and require hash verification).
Sophie (AE): Noted. They also asked whether we support model variants/rollbacks during a canary. Can we pin flint-13B-qlora-v2 as 1.0 in the catalog and set a fallback to flint-7b if mem/latency triggers?
Ajay Patel: Yes — runtime supports automatic fallback to compatible lower-capacity variants if we detect capacity strain, provided tokenization is the same. We need to ensure flint-7b uses same tokenizer and vocab. If not, we only can fallback at routing layer to a different model id — which requires customer acceptance because outputs differ.
Lucas Reed: I validated that flint-7b uses sentencepiece-flint as well. So we can configure a rollout: canary on 1 node, monitor latency and quality (prompt evals), then expand. I'll draft the rollout steps.
Sophie (AE): Perfect. Last ask from them: can we run a 48-hour smoke on Hosted before committing to Dedicated to validate accuracy drift and infra fit?
Ajay Patel: Hosted is possible but note license: since weights have no-commercial-redistribution clause, we can't host their weights on our multi-tenant shared pool. Hosted test would require a customer-scoped hosted instance (isolated bucket + dedicated tenant) — operationally similar to a small Dedicated. We should be explicit in the SOW.
María Gómez: I'll write the SQA entry: "Customer-provided model weights with restrictive license require isolated storage and non-distribution; Redwood will store in customer-scoped object storage and will not publish or redistribute. Hosted test will be on dedicated tenant."
Sophie (AE): Thanks — can you paste that language? I'll include in the security questionnaire.
María Gómez: "Redwood will ingest customer-supplied model weights only into customer-scoped storage accessible to Redwood's dedicated runtime for the POC. Files are not redistributed, and access is logged. For Hosted evaluation, weights will be deployed in an isolated tenant; for Private deployment, weights remain on-customer premises if requested."
Lucas Reed: I'll attach initial perf numbers and a cost spreadsheet later today. For next steps:
- Ajay: confirm any kernel-level changes if we want to optimize qlora-group-size path (ETA 3 days)
- Lucas: perf + cost spreadsheet (ETA EOD)
- María: SQA wording and checklist for the questionnaire (ETA EOD)
- Sophie: I'll send customer the constraints and proposed POC plan with canary and fallback options.
Sophie (AE): Thanks team — I'll update Nimbus and ping when they accept the plan. :thumbsup:
